recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-41401 unless a future work-group decision changes the broader Group-as-actor policy.
issue_request: FHIR-41401 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-core List change request for R6 asking that List.source be able to name a family, modeled as Group, because care may be administered for families acting collectively. Jira records a 2023-12-18 FHIR-I vote by Grahame Grieve/Gino Canessa, 7-0-0.
initial_application: The issue was applied before this reconciliation by git commit 957b26695c13de8dd9d607a39ec3830ef507a359, which added http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Group as a targetProfile for List.source in source/list/structuredefinition-List.xml. Git blame confirms the current Group target line comes from that issue-tagged commit.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists list=List in the active [resources] section, so source/list/structuredefinition-List.xml is build-scope source. FHIR-I minutes from 2023-11-27 record that a decision had been reached that Group can be used as an actor, while noting the related Group-vs-Organization concern in FHIR-41674; 2023-12-18 FHIR-I minutes record the Persuasive motion for FHIR-41401. FHIR-41674 was later resolved Not Persuasive/No Change because other Group definition changes addressed that concern. Jira search found other family/Group actor tickets for different artifacts, but those are separate workgroup/resource decisions and were not decided here.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. The current build-scope List StructureDefinition already includes Group in List.source, and the local combined branch already had the same targetProfile before the audit commit was published.

related_jiras.note: Later Group/Organization boundary concern for Group acting collectively; resolved No Change after other definition updates, so it does not reverse FHIR-41401.
